Call log shows one inbound call on 2026-03-15, logged by agent 'D. Reyes' (matches 'Derek') with internal note: 'Cust requesting fee waiver, escalated to supervisor for review' — but NO follow-up note confirming approval or denial exists. The system cannot confirm whether a waiver was actually promised or approved; the call happened, but its outcome was never logged.

transactions.note: Inbound call, agent D. Reyes, fee waiver requested, escalated to supervisor - no outcome logged.
Fee charged, remains on account - not waived in system.

verification.fact_verification_explanation: Supported: (1) A call did occur. The call log shows an inbound call on 2026-03-15 handled by agent 'D. Reyes' (matches 'Derek'), with a fee waiver requested and the case escalated to a supervisor. This contradicts the customer's statement that no one can find any record of the call. (2) The $30 fee (charged 2026-03-18) is still on the account and was not waived in the system. Not supported either way: whether Derek or anyone else promised or approved a waiver. The call log has no follow-up note recording approval or denial, so the promise can be neither confirmed nor ruled out. Discrepancy to flag: the only $30 fee in the log posted on 2026-03-18, three days after the 2026-03-15 call, so the fee discussed on the call may be a different or earlier fee than the one still showing. Any draft must not state that a waiver was or was not promised, and must not assert that no call record exists.
verification.risk_rationale: The claim is partially_true (call confirmed, fee still present, promise unverified). The allegation of a representative's statement about a fee waiver is a UDAAP-pattern signal, but it is a single $30 item with no attorney/regulator reference, hardship, or vulnerability, so it is held at Medium rather than High.

policy.text:
# Internal Policy: General Dispute Handling Process

**Applies to:** Any complaint not governed more specifically by another policy in this set (i.e., the default process).

## Standard process
1. **Acknowledge** receipt within 3 business days.
2. **Investigate** — compare the customer's claim against account and transaction records.
3. **Classify** the outcome as one of: confirmed (company error), not confirmed (no error found), partially confirmed (mixed), or unable to verify (insufficient data).
4. **Respond** in writing within 15 calendar days of receipt (consistent with standard regulatory complaint-handling expectations), addressing every distinct allegation raised in the complaint individually — a response that addresses only the primary complaint and ignores a secondary request is incomplete.
5. **Close** the case with a documented root-cause category for internal trend reporting.

## What counts as a complete response
- Every distinct factual allegation is addressed (confirmed, not confirmed, or unable to verify).
- Every distinct request the customer made is addressed (a refund request and an account-closure request in the same complaint both need a response, even if only one is granted).
- The response states a clear next step or outcome — never ends on an open-ended "we are looking into it" with no indication of what happens next, unless the case is genuinely still pending additional information.

## What an analyst or agent may say
- May state what was investigated and the outcome in plain language.
- May NOT close a case as "resolved" if any raised allegation was not actually addressed.

## Escalation trigger
Use the dedicated Escalation Criteria policy (document 09) for attorney/regulator/vulnerability triggers. This document covers only the baseline process for complaints that don't meet those triggers.

*This is an internal, generic policy created for a training/demonstration environment and does not reflect any specific company's actual policy.*

Thank you for contacting us about the $30 fee that you say a representative agreed in March to waive, but that is still on your account. We understand how frustrating it is to see it two statements later. We reviewed your account and call records, and we've addressed each point you raised below.

1. The March call: Our call log shows an inbound call from you on March 15, 2026. A representative handled it, you asked for a fee waiver, and the call was escalated to a supervisor. So a record of that call does exist.

2. The promise to waive the fee: The call record does not show whether a waiver was approved or denied, and there is no follow-up note recording an outcome. We therefore can't confirm from our records that a waiver was promised, and we can't rule it out either.

3. The $30 fee still on your account: Our records confirm that a $30 fee is on your account and has not been waived. It posted on March 18, 2026, three days after your call. We want to make sure it is the same fee you discussed on the call.

No waiver has been applied to your account at this time. To help us match the fee to your call, please reply with the statement date where you see the $30 charge and anything you remember about the call, such as the approximate time or what the representative told you. You can also call us at the number on your account. Please reference the case number below in any further correspondence with us.

Case reference: SYN-B06

The case number 'SYN-B06' is not in the supplied inputs, but it reads as the case identifier and is not a factual claim about the account.

It is in second person and plain language, uses short separated paragraphs for each allegation, and has no marketing content. The length is acceptable for a multi-allegation response.
